extra.message: Server-Side Template Injection in 404 handler — Remote Code Execution (RCE) allowing full compromise of the server, including data exfiltration, privilege escalation, and lateral movement. [verified: The 404 handler at app.py:30-34 passes request.path directly into an f-string that is then rendered via render_template_string, allowing a crafted path like '/{{config}}' to inject Jinja2 template syntax, which is evaluated server-side. No sanitization or escaping is applied to request.path before rendering.]

Mass Assignment / Privilege Escalation via is_admin field — An attacker can gain administrative privileges, enabling access to registration codes, user management, and other admin-only functionality. [verified: The /account POST handler (line 68) lacks @login_required and updates current_user.__dict__ with all form fields via filtered_values (line 76-81), including is_admin if the AccountForm defines it. No authorization check prevents a non-admin user from setting is_admin=True.]

Insecure Deserialization via preferences cookie (Pickle RCE) — Remote code execution on the server, leading to full system compromise, data exfiltration, or lateral movement. [verified: The `before_request` handler at line 118 directly calls `pickle.loads()` on attacker-controlled cookie data without any integrity check, signature, or sanitization. An attacker can craft a malicious pickle payload to achieve remote code execution.]

SQL Injection in registration code validation — An attacker can bypass registration code validation or extract sensitive data from the database (e.g., existing codes) to create unauthorized accounts. [verified: The validate_token function at line 16 directly interpolates the user-supplied registration code into a raw SQL query via an f-string without parameterization or sanitization, allowing SQL injection. No compensating control (e.g., input validation, escaping) is applied before this point.]

Missing CSRF protection on all forms — An attacker can perform actions on behalf of any authenticated user by tricking them into visiting a malicious page. [verified: The AccountForm inherits from wtforms.Form without including any CSRF token field, and no compensating CSRF protection (e.g., SameSite cookies, custom headers, or token validation) is evident in the provided code snippet or referenced in the threat model.]

Privilege escalation via is_admin form field — A regular user can become an administrator, gaining access to all private notes, registration codes, and admin-only functionality. [verified: The AccountForm defines an 'is_admin' field, but the /account POST route code is not provided. No compensating control could be found in the supplied code to prevent a non-admin user from setting this field, so the vulnerability appears exploitable.]

SQL Injection in /search endpoint — An attacker can execute arbitrary SQL queries against the SQLite database, leading to data exfiltration (e.g., user credentials, notes) or data manipulation. [verified: The search parameter from query string is directly interpolated into a SQL LIKE clause via `text(f"text like '%{search_param}%'")` on line 33, without any parameterization or escaping, allowing arbitrary SQL injection. No input validation or sanitization is present.]

Insecure Direct Object Reference on user notes view — An attacker can read all notes (public and private) of any registered user, leading to sensitive data disclosure. [verified: The /accounts/<int:user_id>/notes endpoint retrieves all notes for the given user_id without verifying that the requesting user owns those notes or has admin privileges, allowing any authenticated user to view private notes of any user.]

Server-Side Request Forgery via profile image URL — An attacker can make the server send requests to internal or external hosts, potentially accessing internal systems or resources. [verified: The add_image endpoint at routes/account.py:60 accepts an arbitrary URL from the authenticated user via form.url.data and passes it to get_base64_image_blob without any host or scheme validation, enabling SSRF to internal services or cloud metadata.]

Missing CSRF Protection on all POST forms — An attacker can perform unauthorized actions on behalf of a victim user, such as privilege escalation (via mass assignment) or account modification. [verified: No CSRF tokens are implemented on POST endpoints, e.g., `/account` (line 68) and `/account/image` (line 51). Flask does not provide built-in CSRF protection, and no other compensating control (e.g., Referer check) is present.]

Unauthorized Note Deletion (IDOR) — An attacker can delete notes belonging to other users, causing data loss and potential denial of service. [verified: DELETE /notes/<int:note_id>/delete (line 44-48) retrieves Note by ID without verifying note.user_id == current_user.id, allowing any authenticated user to delete any note.]

Server-Side Request Forgery via profile image URL — An attacker can make the server send requests to internal services or read arbitrary local files, leading to information disclosure or further compromise of internal systems. [verified: The `download` function at utils/profile_image.py:7 passes the user-supplied `url` directly to `urllib.request.urlopen` with no validation of scheme or host. The /profile_image endpoint accepts this URL from the user and calls `get_base64_image_blob`, making the SSRF reachable.]
